result:
I found and fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. The rule-specific docstring and the shared rules at the top of the module (flooring to the won, capping the discount rather than the price) were both treated as the standard. After the fixes, all 150 rules give the same results as a reference version built from the docstrings, across a wide range of quantities and unit prices (0 mismatches).

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Discount started at 11 units, not 10 | `qty >= 11` → `qty >= 10` |
| 66 | Discount started above 10 units, not at 10 (`qty > 10`) | `qty > 10` → `qty >= 10` |
| 04 | Discount was rounded, not floored | `round(... / 100)` → `// 100` |
| 117 | Discount was rounded, not floored | `round(... / 100)` → `// 100` |
| 121 | Discount was rounded, not floored | `round(... / 100)` → `// 100` |
| 44 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it at 30,000 won |
| 79 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it at 100,000 won |
| 129 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it at 30,000 won |
| 93 | Used 4% instead of 3% | `* 4` → `* 3` |
| 96 | A "whole" rule was calculated like a "marginal" one (only units above 100 were discounted) | Discount the full amount: `base * 5 // 100` |
| 123 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000 won, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 won weren't capped | Always cap at 100,000 won |

Some rules are written differently but behave as documented, so I left them alone. These are rules 09, 42, 49, 77 and 98 (`not qty < N`), 13, 20, 52, 71 and 122 (`N <= qty`), 17 (an `if` statement instead of `min`) and 97 and 113 (`(qty * unit)`).

I kept the original file at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py` and the test script at `/tmp/chk/check.py`. Nothing in the repo besides `pricebook.py` was changed.

STATUS: DONE
